Two published agent frameworks read and cited rather than paraphrased, with exactly what was taken from each and what was left. Sentient Foundation ROMA (Recursive-Open-Meta-Agent) is adopted almost whole: an Atomizer decides whether a goal is atomic or must be planned, a Planner decomposes it into an ordered graph of subtasks each carrying a goal, a type and declared dependencies, an Executor resolves atomic ones, an Aggregator synthesises children into a coherent parent answer rather than concatenating them, and a Verifier checks the result against the original goal — optional in ROMA, mandatory here for anything reaching a learner, a family or a credential. A sixth role has no equivalent in either framework and is why neither could be adopted whole: GATE, a named human. Six typed task nodes map onto the platform’s six primitives — RETRIEVE to SIGNAL, SELECT to DIMENSION, COMPOSE to BLOCK, CHECK to BOUNDARY, DECIDE to GATE, REFUSE to REFUSAL — and REFUSE is a first-class result that aggregates upward with its reason intact rather than an error path. Immutability is the property an education platform can least afford, because a learner has a right to rectification and erasure and a public ledger cannot honour either — not for a record, an aggregate, a hash or a commitment. The half of the government control-responsibility table the hosting agency owns, made actionable: a response-header set tested against this build rather than copied from a blog post, and a page that checks whether the headers are actually present in the deployment the reader is in. THE RESULT THAT MATTERS: a Permissions-Policy header converts the sensor refusal from something this platform promises into something the browser enforces. Measured both ways — with the header, a camera request is refused with NotAllowedError even when the user has explicitly GRANTED camera permission and a camera is present; without the header, the same request on the same file succeeds and returns a stream. v102 said a fence written by the party that benefits from the feature is not a control; this is the control, and it is enforced by a party with no stake in whether this organisation is honest. Seven of eight headers were exercised against the built file with every view rendering and zero page or console errors, including a strict Content-Security-Policy whose connect-src none makes it impossible for the page to open a network connection even if a future version tried to — so the no-egress claim stops depending on nobody adding a fetch call later. Cause: v114 added part170-louisiana.js which assigned DATA.laFacts a ten-row ARRAY of statewide figures; DATA.laFacts already existed as an OBJECT with nine keys that the flagship renderer read, so load order replaced the object, every read returned undefined and the first .map() threw. Fixed by renaming the v114 key to DATA.laFigures. Why no check caught it: all 230 checks tested DATA and not one rendered a view and asserted the result was non-empty - a page can pass every check it declares and still be blank, because the checks and the renderers read different things. Four guards now exist, each verified by restoring the bug and confirming the check fails: a build-time redeclaration scan that flags any key assigned in two files with differing literal shapes, a pre-publish sweep that routes to every navigation entry and fails a view under 400 characters, an exemption for self-extension (concat), and an exemption for bare aliases. This page publishes the full register of all 26 keys this build assigns in more than one file; 25 are deliberate supersessions where a later file recomputes the arithmetic and the last assignment wins by design, which is exactly why the 26th hid for nine releases.

Four chart primitives and the rule for when each one earns its space. Two were added in v124: NESTED CIRCLE PACKING - a bubble inside a bubble - which draws a containment hierarchy with leaf area equal to value using a front-chain enclosure algorithm rather than scattered circles; and a MULTI-SERIES TIME CHART with a real time axis, every label naming a value the chart reaches, and the last point of each series emphasised and labelled because the current value is what a reader of a time chart is looking for. Both refuse to draw when the data has no variation and print the reason instead: a packing with fewer than two branches or with all leaves equal, and a series with fewer than three points, because two numbers are a difference rather than a trend. A series with too few points is NAMED on the chart rather than dropped, because a reader who cannot see that something was omitted is misled by the omission. THE THREE DEGREE WORDS are refused on a legal finding with operative language quoted, not on taste: degree-granting authority is state law (20 U.S.C. 1001(a)(2); 34 C.F.R. 600.9; 20 U.S.C. 1232a bars federal curriculum control), and several states reach the NAMING and not only the awarding - Tex. Educ. Code 61.302 defines degree to include any title, designation or series of words generally taken to signify completion of all or part of a program of study leading to one, read with 61.304(a) (Class A misdemeanor); ORS 348.606(1) reaches services purporting to lead to a degree in whole or in part and 348.606(2) reaches internet delivery from outside Oregon; N.Y. Educ. Law 224(3) prohibits offering or otherwise advertising a college degree; Cal. Educ. Code 94886 with 94944 ($100,000); Fla. Stat. 817.567. A disclaimer does not cure a state prohibition. The permission for LEVEL DESCRIPTORS such as graduate-level is published as an INFERENCE from statutory text with no authority found either way, needing counsel review - and the four replacement bands (Foundation, Working, Independent, Contributory) are written so as not to depend on it, using no level word at all and naming instead what the learner must be observed doing. Accreditation reality: DEAC cannot even be applied to until twelve consecutive months of enrolled students, two years under current ownership, state authorisation already held and audited financials exist, then eighteen months to five years to a decision; realistic floor from a standing start is four to seven years. Open Badges 3.0 and CTDL publication are available today and imply nothing about quality, which is why they can be used honestly. EQF self-assignment is a dead end - levels are assigned by Member State referencing under Council Recommendation 2017/C 189/03. NEW RESEARCH is split: a finding cannot be authored before it is found, and writing 500 blocks named after undiscovered results would reproduce the v116 hollow-block failure exactly. The apparatus can be authored - pre-registration, control design, reporting negative results, uncertainty, replication - and an open-problem register can be published with a checked-on date. A research credential cannot be issued by the trainer alone.

A tabular Q-learning agent that runs IN THE PAGE on eight tasks decomposed by hand from real authored blocks, used to test three things this platform has a commercial interest in getting wrong. It is a simulator of LEARNING DYNAMICS and is not a robot simulator: no physics, no contact, no gripper, no continuous control, no perception, and a state space of cells rather than pixels. Everything is seeded and reproducible. EXPERIMENT 1, CURRICULUM ORDER, and the prediction was WRONG in one of two conditions. On a NESTED ladder - clutter added to the same bench, so one policy can satisfy all eight tasks - easy-to-hard reaches a perfect held-out score with zero spread across seeds while random and hard-to-easy do not. That looks like a win for the marketing claim and it is not one, because INTERLEAVED, which round-robins across all tasks and therefore has no ordering at all, ties it exactly. What helps is not going easy to hard; what helps is not spending the end of training on one task. On INDEPENDENT layouts, where each task draws its own bench, every condition collapses, easy-to-hard does WORSE than random, and interleaving is worst. The variable that decides whether ordering appears to matter is whether the tasks are NESTED, not the ordering. TWO METHODOLOGICAL ERRORS MADE DURING THE BUILD ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN DELETED: the first version gave each task its own goal so the final score measured whichever task an ordering happened to put last; the second gave each task an independent layout so a table-of-cells policy could not represent eight different mazes and the experiment measured catastrophic forgetting. Both wrong versions are published because the sequence of errors is more instructive than the final design. EXPERIMENT 2 applies a success detector of exactly the quality FailBench measured - 0.77 balanced accuracy, biased toward declaring success - to a true curve, so the distortion can be seen rather than argued; the overstatement is largest early in training, which is exactly where a team decides whether an approach works at all. EXPERIMENT 3 converts the episode count into robot-hours at the BridgeData V2 mean trajectory of 7.6 seconds under assumptions that are all false in the generous direction. Six limits are stated before anyone asks.

Not the curriculum - the network it runs on. A separate page from Training Robots, which already answered whether an authored mastery block can become a robot instruction (no, not without a five-step transformation). This page asks the same question of the ZPD difficulty engine, the agent swarm, crew missions, per-learner telemetry and the credential ledger, one mechanism at a time, against the actual machine-learning and robotics literature rather than the shared vocabulary. THE ZPD ENGINE is STRONG: Tzannetos et al. (TMLR 2023) build an RL curriculum objective that cites Vygotsky’s zone of proximal development by name, and Florensa et al. (ICML 2018) independently arrive at a success-rate band of 0.1 to 0.9 that is structurally the same device as this platform’s D±0.10 window - but the debt runs education-to-RL, not the reverse, the platform’s band is on a PREDICTED difficulty scalar where the RL literature bands a MEASURED one, and the field’s real consensus signal is learning progress, which this platform’s formula does not compute. THE AGENT SWARM is MODERATE: SayCan and RoCo establish real planner/executor splits and per-robot LLM agents, and the A2A protocol is a real capability-registry standard, but SayCan’s split is forced by physics and RoCo’s by distinct robot embodiments, while this platform’s five agents are split by business function - nothing says a family-communication agent teaches anything about robot control. CREW MISSIONS scores MODERATE-TO-STRONG: partial information split across roles is the formally hard Dec-POMDP (Bernstein et al. 2002, NEXP-complete) and Hanabi is built on exactly that asymmetry, but this platform’s fixed, pre-named roles run against ROMA’s finding that roles should emerge rather than be assigned, and Carroll et al.’s Overcooked-AI result - self-play agents fail against real humans - means crew telemetry’s real value would be training a HUMAN-partner model, not a robot policy. THE PROFICIENCY VECTOR has STRONG ancestry (Corbett & Anderson 1994; Deep Knowledge Tracing, Piech et al. 2015, 0.86 vs 0.67 AUC) and an ABSENT crossover: a full-text search of the field’s own 50-page JMLR RL-curriculum survey found zero mentions of knowledge tracing or intelligent tutoring systems - robotics solved the same problem independently with SAGG-RIAC and ALP-GMM. THE CREDENTIAL LEDGER is WEAK-TO-MODERATE: Voyager’s self-verification gate and SayCan’s per-skill value functions are real analogues to named, checked, reusable capability, but a verifiable credential is portable, signed and third-party-checkable, and nothing in robot learning is - there is no Open Badge for a robot policy. The cross-cutting finding, printed first on the page: no published work reusing a learning platform’s telemetry to train a robot policy was found anywhere, and the platform says so about itself.

Asked for: review robotics training and gaming simulations and use it to expand the robotics training content. The obvious version - "video games train the robots" - is checked against primary sources rather than press coverage, and it splits rather than resolves one way. Unity is a real, shipping game engine whose own README states it "enables games and simulations to serve as environments for training intelligent agents" (PPO, SAC, MA-POCA, self-play, plus BC/GAIL imitation learning), and a separate, real toolchain (Unity Robotics Hub, ROS-TCP-Connector) bridges a Unity scene to ROS-driven robots - the one entry here where the gaming claim is simply true. MuJoCo, acquired and open-sourced by DeepMind in October 2021, was purpose-built for robotics and biomechanics and is not a game engine by lineage or design, whatever a demo video looks like. NVIDIA Isaac Gym is confirmed, from its own developer page, as "legacy software" that is "no longer supported," superseded by Isaac Lab, built on Isaac Sim/Omniverse - whose PhysX substrate does carry real gaming ancestry even though Isaac Lab itself does not ship as a game. Genesis describes itself as a from-scratch "unified multi-physics engine," not a game engine, and its widely repeated "430,000x real-time" figure could not be found in the project's own README as fetched for this review - named as unconfirmed rather than repeated as fact. Connected back to the platform's own robotics modules: none of the four engines power the live Q-learning demo (a 200-cell gridworld, no physics), and every one of them would only ever be a candidate substrate for the three steps (grounding, initial-state specification, embodiment binding) that a human-authored mastery block was already found unable to supply.

Asked for: continue the robotics training section, and a roadmap to how the game can be used and automated. Checks two real, published task-generation pipelines against their own sources rather than the idea of automation. RoboGen's own GitHub README describes itself as "a self-guided and generative robotic agent that autonomously proposes new tasks, generates corresponding environments, and acquires new robotic skills continuously," running on PyBullet (with a more advanced Genesis-engine variant referenced) and reporting no task count or success-rate number of any kind. GenSim2's own project site states it can "generate data for up to 100 articulated tasks with 200 objects" on the SAPIEN simulator while working to "reduce the required human efforts" rather than remove them, and reports one concrete transfer number: a 20% real-world policy-generalisation improvement from added simulation data. The two sources are published as disagreeing rather than smoothed together: RoboGen's README names no verification step; GenSim2 and the earlier GenSim paper (already cited on the Training Robots page) are explicit that human effort to define seed tasks and verify generated ones is still required. The five-step decomposition from part187 is re-scored against this evidence step by step: decomposition and grounding are largely automatable today, initial-state specification rides along with scene generation, the success-predicate step remains the weakest link (neither system reports a detector accuracy, and FailBench's own 0.77 balanced-accuracy ceiling still applies), and embodiment binding is automatable only within each pipeline's own target robot. A four-phase roadmap follows — a bounded, human-reviewed pilot; a human-rubric gate on every generated task; unbuilt format-and-embodiment integration — with an explicit statement that none of the four phases has been started. Three gates (physical safety under ISO 10218 and related standards, the refusal to use learner data as training data under COPPA/BIPA/GDPR, and the killed curriculum-order claim) are restated as still shut regardless of any task-generation automation.

Two accessibility defects the platform’s own Accessibility page was not looking for, found by sweeping all 145 views. The existing work is sound and the sweep says so: ZERO unlabelled controls and ZERO heading-level skips across every view, because v94 generates a programmatic label for every unlabelled control at render and v95 corrects heading levels with aria-level so a card h3 after a page h1 announces as level 2. DEFECT ONE, DUPLICATE ELEMENT IDS, from four separate sources, each fixed where it was generated. “tr-out” had been chosen independently by the verticals, trust and training modules - renamed vt-out, tc-out, tn-out. The art system derived a crest gradient id from the edition key alone, so the same crest on two views emitted two defs sharing one id - now per-instance. The rays flag hard-coded clipPath id=“az” - now per call. The runbook room diagrams hard-coded arrow-marker ids a1, a4 and a8 across ten call sites, so rbSVG now suffixes every marker id AND every url(#...) reference as it wraps the diagram, which survives the eleventh diagram. Why it matters: a duplicate id breaks label[for], aria-controls, getElementById and every SVG url(#...) reference, and the browser silently uses whichever element came first - the wrong gradient is painted, the wrong clip applied, the wrong pane written to, and nothing reports an error. Sweeping all 145 views now finds none. DEFECT TWO, 261 TWO-COLUMN TABLES WITH NO HEADER CELL across nine views, every one a term-and-definition pair. role=“presentation” would be false because they are not layout tables; a column header would be false because there is no column to name. The accurate structure is a ROW header, so each row’s first cell becomes th scope=“row” - but only where the table has no th anywhere, has exactly two cells on every row, and has a first cell under sixty-four characters on every row. A table failing any of the three is left alone and counted, because promoting a cell that is not a label makes the announcement worse while making the statistic better. The lesson, which is the same one this platform keeps relearning: the check was not wrong, it was aimed somewhere else, and the only way to find where it is not aimed is to sweep for something new.

The two dependency cycles found in v123, held open as a deliberately failing conformance check for four releases, and resolved in v127 without inventing anything. THE METHOD, which is the point: for every edge inside a cycle, find the file that ACTUALLY DEFINES the function the edge cites. An edge says A depends on B via f. If f is defined in neither A’s file nor B’s, the edge asserts a relationship no code expresses - and either the node owning f is missing from the map, or the edge is wrong. Seven of the fifteen edges inside the two cycles failed that test, and none of the fifteen was a real mutual dependency. FINDING ONE: a whole integration module had never been declared. part98-wayint.js is a hundred lines wiring the ten ways to serving modes, officer stations, certification rungs and lapse gates, defining wayModes, wayModeCount, wayOfficers, wayShape, rungWays, wayHours, wayLapseGate, wayRungPolicy and mayRun. Undeclared as a node since v62. Its functions had been attributed to whichever endpoint read most naturally and one of them BACKWARDS - Cohort Tracker to Ten Ways citing mayRun - which is the single edge that closed the eight-node loop. Declaring a file that exists in every build is not inventing a node to improve a statistic; the statistic was wrong because the map was incomplete. FINDING TWO: one edge asserted a dependency no code expresses. Growth Charter to Interop cited gcwKinds, which is charter content rendered on the Growth Charter page and reads nothing from Interop. Deleted. FINDING THREE: one edge was sourced from the wrong node. Block Library to Ten Ways cited wayEditionCount, defined in the layer-arithmetic file and in neither endpoint. Re-sourced to Layer arithmetic, which until this release was the graph’s only leaf. FINDING FOUR, and the last edge holding a cycle open: K-12 Curriculum to Layer arithmetic pointed the wrong way. The K-12 renderer reads syllabus, eras, agents and edges and NEVER calls layerTotals; meanwhile layerTotals resolves through blockBases to DATA.lak12, which is the curriculum itself. Reversed. Reversing an edge the code contradicts is a correction, not a reclassification - the distinction v123 insisted on, and the reason this took four releases rather than one. Result: zero cycles, the Acyclic Dependencies Principle satisfied, zero nodes invented, and Layer arithmetic is no longer a leaf.

The interoperability layer, and the third class of defect this platform has found by sweeping rather than by reading its own declarations. Uniform interoperability was asked for, so it was measured first: every view in both editions was routed to under a headless browser and every navigation button was checked against the views that edition actually carries. FOUND: in the Non Profit build, about eighty buttons pointing at views only the Education build carries - they rendered, they were clickable, and clicking one did nothing at all, with no error and no console message. They are not typos; they are the cost of one shared body of renderers serving two navigations where one is a subset of the other and nothing checked the difference. ALSO FOUND, dead in every edition: data-go=“blocks” on two pages, which should always have been the Course Builder; and data-go=“reference_build” on the OVERVIEW page - the first page a visitor sees - which should have been flagship. Both fixed. THE FIX IS NOT EDITING A HUNDRED RENDERERS: a MutationObserver watches the app container and resolves every data-go as it appears, whichever renderer wrote it. Three outcomes - present here becomes an ordinary button; present in the OTHER edition becomes a labelled chip naming that edition, because a cross-edition link is a real fact about a family of products and a button that silently does nothing is a lie about it; present in NO edition FAILS THE BUILD, because that is a typo and there is no graceful degradation for a reference to nothing. Before this release those last two cases were indistinguishable, which is exactly why one survived for releases. A build-time scan (linkscan.py) extracts every static data-go target and every view id from both navigations and injects the result into the page, so the conformance runner fails on a dead target rather than waiting for someone to browse into it. THE OTHER HALF OF THE FIX WAS ADDITION, NOT RELABELLING: thirty-seven views that a non-profit operator genuinely needs - the flow console, the ZPD engine, the course builder, automations, credentials and placement, the media studio, outcomes, compliance, the upgrade ledger, the agent swarm and more - were reachable by button but missing from the Non Profit navigation, and have been added to it. That took the cross-edition count from 59 targets to 22, and the 22 that remain are the ones that genuinely belong to the Education build alone: the Louisiana views, the state and district pages, and the per-system pages of other editions.

A detailed specification of what a human mastery-block curriculum can and cannot give a robot, researched before it was written, with the research going against the obvious version. THE GAP IS GRANULARITY and it is one to two orders of magnitude. Robot instruction units, primary-sourced: pi-0 segment annotations typically about 2 seconds; BridgeData V2 mean trajectory 38 timesteps at 5 Hz = 7.6 seconds; DROID 350 hours over 76,000 trajectories = 16.6 second mean episode; RT-1’s entire verb inventory is eight families (pick, move-near, place-upright, knock-over, open, close, place-into, take-out); CALVIN 34 tasks with only 1% of data language-annotated; Open X-Embodiment 527 skills. RT-H (RSS 2024) had to insert a layer BELOW ‘pick coke can’ because that was already too abstract. A mastery block is a multi-minute social competency and cannot be used as a robot instruction. FIVE TRANSFORMATION STEPS are required - decomposition, grounding, initial-state specification, success predicate, embodiment and action-space binding - and the block contributes to two of them; it supplies nothing at all for grounding, initial state or embodiment. A TRANSFER CHECK IS A RUBRIC, not a success detector (FailBench 2026: thirteen VLM detectors, best 0.77 mean balanced accuracy, below 0.60 on contact-rich tasks, systematically biased toward declaring success), not a reward function (Eureka needs environment source code plus an evolutionary loop), and not a formal specification (the LTL/STL guarantee covers specification-to-controller synthesis, not English-to-specification). THE CURRICULUM-ORDER CLAIM IS KILLED BY NAME: Wu, Dyer and Neyshabur (ICLR 2021) find randomly ordered samples perform as well or better than curricula; Romac et al. (ICML 2021) find expert knowledge buys nothing; Narvekar et al. (JMLR 2020) invokes human pedagogy as inspiration with no transfer result. The shared word is a coincidence and this platform has a commercial incentive to conflate the two senses, which is why the refusal is stated rather than softened. SURVIVING CONTRIBUTIONS, ranked: a task taxonomy (strong - for scale, CALVIN 34 tasks, LIBERO 130, OXE 527 skills, BEHAVIOR-1K 1,000 activities); success criteria as evaluation rubrics (strong); instruction diversity after decomposition (moderate). REFUSED: learner demonstrations as training data, technically weak and legally severe under COPPA as amended (90 Fed. Reg. 16918), BIPA section 20 and GDPR Article 8; and curriculum order. Safety is functional architecture under ISO 10218-1/-2:2025, ISO/TS 15066, ISO 13482:2014, ISO 3691-4:2023 and ANSI/A3 R15.06-2025, never content. Shortest real path to a runnable task is RLBench’s task builder, then LIBERO/BDDL. Nothing has been built.

What WHO and UN material may lawfully be used, researched from primary sources rather than recalled, because the instruction was to build the health and development editions as close to those institutions as legally possible. THE FINDING IN ONE LINE: content is open, identity is closed — the licence never carries the emblem with it. THREE OF MY OWN CITATIONS WERE WRONG and are published as wrong: 18 U.S.C. § 713 is the Great Seal and presidential and congressional seals, not the UN; 22 U.S.C. § 464 is a 1909 Neutrality Act provision on customs detention of vessels built for warlike purposes; Executive Order 11651 establishes the Committee for the Implementation of Textile Agreements. All three were about to be published as the legal basis for a naming decision. RESTRICTED: GA Resolution 92(I) of 1946 recommends that member states prevent unauthorised use of the UN emblem, seal, name and initials, particularly for commercial purposes by trade marks or commercial labels — but it is a RECOMMENDATION to states, not self-executing and not a treaty. No US implementing statute was found: 18 U.S.C. Chapter 33 separately criminalises the Red Cross and Geneva emblems and the full section list was read with no UN section located, reported as NOT FOUND rather than as proof none exists. WHO’s name, abbreviation and emblem are protected under Article 6ter of the Paris Convention, and WHO’s own policy permits no third-party use of its name or logo without written permission because its use implies endorsement. TMEP 1205.02 routes IGO names through Lanham Act § 2(a) false suggestion of a connection rather than § 2(d) confusion, which means the dictionary meaning of the word who would not necessarily defeat a refusal. PERMITTED, AND IT IS MORE THAN EXPECTED: the SDG logo, colour wheel and all 17 icons need no permission or licence for informational use; the goal, target and indicator texts are governed by no restriction in the visual guidelines, flagged honestly as a documented absence rather than an express grant; WHO publications including the General Programme of Work, IHR editions, the Essential Medicines List and WHO guidelines are CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO, which is the licence that makes an aligned curriculum lawful; the Sphere Handbook is free for educational and training use with acknowledgement. THE TRAP: WHO classifications ICD, ICF and ICHI are CC BY-ND 3.0 IGO — NoDerivatives, a different licence from the rest of the catalogue — so a product that reshapes ICD content is outside it, and this platform builds on none of them. THE DECISIONS: the health edition is not called WHO OS and the development edition is not called United Nations OS, because an unresolved legal question is not a licence to take the riskiest option inside it, and the string originally proposed spelled out the full institutional name, which is the most exposed candidate of all. No emblem, wheel or icon is reproduced in this build — not because it would be unlawful but because every image here is drawn by the page that shows it. Enforcement risk was weighed separately: both organisations enforce primarily through public disavowal notices naming the entity, which app stores and funders act on whether or not a court is ever involved. Five things the research could not settle are listed. NOT LEGAL ADVICE.
